issue_plan.name: Collect authentic Go acceptance outcomes
issue_plan.summary: Complete #537 in two ordered pull requests: first the authentic Go event producer and reusable host transport, then lifecycle validation and conversion to acceptance evidence through a separate local RunAcceptance fixture. Each boundary gets real-process tests covering exact identities, command semantics, hostile diagnostics, failures, interruption and cleanup. Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and the README status at each step; broader shared integration in step 2 of #536 and prepared-Docker runtime transport remain pending. The merger confirms D-0321 and records the new runtime-collection decisions before dependent work proceeds.

issues.title: Produce authentic Go testing events through a reusable host transport
issues.body:
This is the first of two changes completing #537, the local runtime-collection step of #536/#534 within #523/#513/#452. Add a production Go framework event producer and reusable host-owned transport under internal/plumbing, building on go_acceptance.go, go_discovery.go and repository_acceptance.go. Deliver a working producer exercised by actual Go processes. The next planned issue validates and converts its stream into RepositoryAcceptanceEvidence through RunAcceptance, separating framework instrumentation and process ownership from acceptance attribution for review.

Production boundary and authentic events:

- The producer, helper/framework hook, preparation and protocol are host-owned production Go code using only the pinned local Go toolchain and standard library offline, without Python, installation, downloads, network or host caches.
- Define explicit transport operations for private helper/source staging, subprocess preparation and launch, an independent event channel, separate stdout/stderr diagnostics, process wait, bounded drain/shutdown and release. The transport supplies mechanics; it cannot infer test outcomes or supply a substitute reporter. A later prepared-Docker transport must use this identical producer and, once added, the identical collector without reimplementing either.
- Add a distinct local process fixture in new Go test files. It may launch processes and own private temporary storage, but must run the production producer and real Go tools, never manufacture framework events, JSON evidence or verdicts. Do not extend discovery-only fixtures to execute tests.
- Obtain test starts and terminal results directly from Go testing lifecycle hooks through a channel independent of BOTH workload stdout and stderr. Parsing go test output, test2json output, lifecycle-looking text or framing-looking diagnostics into another record format does not qualify. Compilation, process exit and synthetic failure or runner markers cannot stand in for a framework terminal event.
- Preserve Go testing behavior, including TestMain, initialization, nested tests, parallel children, skips, assertion failures and panic handling. Instrumentation must preserve acceptance bytes, ordinary production sources and dependencies, build constraints and ordinary/external test packages. Retain exact runtime parent/child names and sufficient ordered lifecycle to distinguish an absent child from a discovered parent, and to validate nested and parallel completion later. Preserve explanations for real pass, failure and skip. A real assertion failure or panic with framework failure completion is distinct from an abrupt exit without terminal events.

Selection, ownership and binding:

- Reuse production Select and Discover; add no alternate selection, package-loading or declaration policy. Select refuses unsupported commands before any preparation or execution. Before production event collection, real package loading, verbatim-source/inclusion/declaration checks and compilation must succeed. Wrong-file, excluded-file, duplicate declarations, wrong module or other discovery failures must prevent producer invocation.
- Execute each selector separately from its captured owning part directory with the safely narrowed test_one arguments. Preserve local module ownership, ordinary local package dependencies and the discovered Go import path; another package, file, module or part must never supply the requested selection.
- Carry the host's fresh InvocationID, complete (part, framework, file, selector) identity, verbatim acceptance source, SourceDigest and captured ExecutionDigest from selection/discovery through the production stream boundary, using the discovered import path. A top-level declaration does not establish that the selected subtest exists. Candidate configuration and diagnostic claims supply no authority.
- Preserve the full docs/factory.md grammar: direct literal go test; exactly one -run placeholder, separate or equal form, whose entire value is {test} or ^{test}$; omitted scope or exactly one clean inclusive ., ./dir, ./... or ./dir/... scope. Never widen scope, enter Go-skipped recursive directories or cross module boundaries. Independently regexp-escape and anchor every slash-separated selector component; shell-looking names remain literal arguments.
- Preserve both value spellings, order, boundaries and semantics of -tags; nonnegative -timeout including 0; a single positive -parallel, -p or -cpu value; -shuffle off/on or a signed integer seed; -mod readonly/vendor; -count exactly 1, adding it when absent; and bare or =true/=false -short, -v, -race and -trimpath. Do not omit, override or refuse a previously supported flag to make instrumentation work. Continue refusing unsupported/repeated/conflicting flags, wrappers, executable paths, opaque commands, file/import-path/multiple scopes and all other unsupported forms before preparation. Host instrumentation must not admit candidate-specified hooks or overlays.

Context and ownership:

- Every validation, read, package load, compile, helper preparation and runtime subprocess inherits the caller's context and remaining allowance. No operation starts a new whole-run or test-phase budget. Design for the existing twelve-minute run and single ten-minute test phase, including shorter caller/preparer limits, without adding a scheduler.
- Make ownership explicit for resources acquired before preparation/start failure, including a handle returned alongside an error. The disposable part environment owns resources until shared-lifecycle Close; release and drain work must be bounded and usable under uncanceled cleanup after execution cancellation. Stop and reap real subprocesses and bound pipe drains; retain infrastructure/cleanup errors and unfinished lifecycle rather than synthesizing completion.
- Preserve private regular-file staging, safe ancestors and verified offline dependencies. Never change the original checkout or caller's candidate; execute verbatim pinned bytes even when a candidate copy has normalized line endings. Local tests use isolated temporary caches, not user caches.

Required default Go tests:

- Use small standard-library-only temporary modules and actual loading, compilation and execution through the production producer. No Docker, network, opt-in or substituted JSON producer is permitted for outcome tests. Demonstrate one unchanged acceptance source failing a real assertion against a base production file and passing after changing only that production file.
- Cover top-level and exact nested selectors, parallel children, regexp punctuation and shell-looking names; prefix, sibling and parameter-case neighbors; absent children; repeated names across packages/modules/parts; an external test package; included/excluded build tags; and ordinary local production imports. Check supported flags through real executions as well as literal argument observations, including both spellings, explicit false booleans, timeout 0, count 1, shuffle, vendor/readonly, race and trimpath semantics. Preserve Go's own treatment of captured flags instead of quietly dropping them.
- Observe real passing, failing and skipped terminal events with explanations. Cover zero-test execution, absent selectors, TestMain exiting before m.Run, nonzero abrupt exits before and during a test, panic completion, and bounded interruption of an actual running process. Distinguish no start from started but unfinished work. Cancellation must also bound preparation, package loading, compilation and helper work; test partial-start ownership and cleanup.
- Print misleading PASS/FAIL, lifecycle lines, test2json JSON, runner records, framing-looking bytes and complete binding-looking records to BOTH stdout and stderr during initialization, TestMain and tests. Include genuine pass with false failure, genuine failure with false success, and incomplete execution with both claims. Compare with uncorrupted controls, prove diagnostic bytes remain diagnostics, and retain them for inspection. The second issue extends these cases through evidence conversion.

Compatibility and documentation:
Inspection found no existing test or command expectation that needs weakening. Keep internal/plumbing/go_selection_accept_test.go, go_discovery_accept_test.go, go_discovery_regression_test.go and go_lifecycle_accept_test.go unchanged. In particular, goEnvironment527.Run still allows go list/env/version and go test -c but refuses test execution; its no-collector controls remain. The trusted go_discovery_regression_test.go collector still tests discovery-to-collector binding only. Add the runtime transport fixture separately. If later inspection reveals an existing test requiring an edit, its implementation plan must explicitly list that file and explain the necessity before ratification; do not silently broaden scope.

Preserve the existing acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go, acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go, native_execution_accept_test.go, native_identity_accept_test.go, other native hash/lock regressions and built-in sandbox coverage. Add no mandatory start/collector capability to trusted fake adapters or Run/ReadFile/Close-only environments.

Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README.md's adapter-status sentence to describe the implemented event producer and local transport accurately, with evidence conversion still pending until the next planned issue. Keep the README at most 400 lines and link to docs/factory.md for command grammar, evidence and transport detail. Every new or changed SPEC bullet cites recorded decisions. Keep configured planning admission, default and candidate-controlled adapter registration, external plumbing and production pytest/Vitest/Jest disabled. Preserve legacy Go execution, hashes and locks without inferred metadata or migration. Do not modify .github/ or decisions/.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311 (#484), D-0314 (#503), D-0316 (#515), and D-0321, the recorded #527 selection/discovery contract. The latter exists at decisions/journal/D-0321.jsonl; do not invent a replacement ID.

Merger work: confirm D-0321 and record the new producer/transport decision before dependent work proceeds; plumbing builds cannot write decisions/. Genuinely unavailable Docker/network checks and decision recording alone do not require a builder repair. Default real-Go tests are required, and any affected opt-in real Python/TLAPS suites remain required in pull-request CI. This issue does not implement the broader shared integration already assigned to step 2 of #536 or the prepared-Docker runtime transport assigned to the separate second step of #534.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Validate Go runtime lifecycles and return local acceptance evidence
issues.body:
Complete #537 after the preceding producer/transport issue merges. #537 is the local runtime-collection step of #536/#534 within #523/#513/#452. Using the predecessor's production events, independent channel and separate real-process fixture, add lifecycle validation and conversion to RepositoryAcceptanceEvidence under internal/plumbing. Exercise production Select, Discover and collection through RepositoryAcceptanceEnvironment.RunAcceptance. Complete all local collector requirements here; broader shared integration is already assigned to step 2 of #536.

Production collector:

- RunAcceptance in the separate local environment delegates to the production collector. The fixture owns only process/file/channel mechanics, never a reporter, inferred outcomes, manufactured JSON evidence or a substitute collector. A later prepared-Docker transport must reuse this identical producer and collector unchanged.
- Reuse GoRepositoryAcceptanceAdapter.Select and Discover in go_acceptance.go and go_discovery.go and their existing shared-lifecycle validation. Each selector runs separately in its captured owning part directory after real package loading, exact source inclusion/bytes/declaration checks and compilation. Unsupported commands must stop at Select before preparation; failed discovery must prevent collector invocation and runtime attribution. Do not add a second selector or discovery policy.
- Pin the host's fresh InvocationID, full (part, framework, file, selector) identity, discovered Go import path, verbatim source and SourceDigest, and captured ExecutionDigest throughout. Check these bindings before converting records and returning them through the shared evidence boundary. Never attribute another file, package, module or part, even when names match.
- Require exactly one requested selection, one authentic start for that exact runtime test and one authentic terminal result, with sufficient authentic parent/child lifecycle to validate nested and parallel tests. Do not confuse interleaved parallel siblings with illegal reordering. An ancestor, prefix, sibling, different parameter case or parameterized family cannot stand in for an exact requested child. Discovering the parent alone proves no child's existence.
- Reject duplicate, stale, contradictory, reordered, truncated, missing or mismatched lifecycle and bindings. Include tests that mutate captured real producer streams, compare each with its uncorrupted control, and show that terminal-without-start, duplicate starts, child/ancestor substitution, conflicting terminals, stale InvocationID, changed source/execution digests and every identity/package mismatch cannot qualify. Such corruption tests supplement actual outcome tests and never replace the real producer.
- Valid completed pass, assertion failure, framework-completed panic and selected skip become kind test with status passed, failed or skipped and retained explanations. Selected skip qualifies neither a candidate pass nor a base failure. Zero-test success, absent selectors/children, TestMain exiting before m.Run, abrupt nonzero exit, interruption or missing terminal events cannot establish completion; preserve refused, not_run and running statuses with reasons as appropriate.
- Tool/helper preparation, package/discovery and compilation failures are setup/refusal outcomes, including compilation against a proposed API. Do not manufacture a test failure from a compiler error or process exit. Precise compiler attribution remains in #523's already ordered later issue outside #534; preserve the existing attributable compile-failure contract of trusted fake adapters.
- Keep Go's authentic-start requirement inside the production Go runtime path. Do not impose it on repositoryEvidence's existing trusted fake-adapter contract or on environments implementing only Run/ReadFile/Close. Preserve valid partial evidence and diagnostics while retaining infrastructure errors that veto qualification.

Command, source and transport compatibility:
Preserve the entire supported docs/factory.md grammar and actual flag semantics from the predecessor and #527: direct literal go test; exactly one separate/equal -run placeholder whose value is {test} or ^{test}$; omitted scope or one inclusive clean ., ./dir, ./... or ./dir/... scope, safely narrowed without widening, Go-skipped recursive subdirectories or crossing modules. Each slash component is independently regexp-escaped and anchored, and shell-looking names stay arguments. Keep both value spellings and boundaries for -tags, nonnegative -timeout including 0, one positive -parallel/-p/-cpu value, -shuffle off/on or integer seed, -mod readonly/vendor, -count exactly 1 with absent count added, and bare or =true/=false -short/-v/-race/-trimpath. Refuse unsupported/repeated/conflicting flags, wrappers, opaque commands, file/import-path/multiple scopes and other unsupported forms before preparation. Do not silently drop or override flags for instrumentation.

Preserve ordinary and external packages, local module ownership and production dependencies, build constraints, verified offline dependencies, private regular-file staging and safe ancestors. Run the verbatim acceptance source even when a candidate stores normalized line endings. Neither diagnostics nor candidate configuration can alter source, identity, execution policy or registration. The producer/helper uses only the pinned Go toolchain and standard library offline, with no Python, installation, downloads, network or host caches.

All validation, loading, compilation, helper preparation and runtime operations inherit the context and remaining allowance supplied by the existing lifecycle. The collector never starts a fresh twelve-minute whole run or ten-minute test phase; shorter caller and preparer limits remain effective. No scheduler is added. Test cancellation and bounded subprocess/drain shutdown, including partial preparation/start failure, with explicit ownership through the disposable environment and shared Close. Cleanup uses the existing bounded uncanceled allowance and must not leave child processes or private resources behind. The local collector's inherited deadlines and resource contract must work here; broader multi-part base/candidate, allowance and queue integration remains step 2 of #536.

Required default acceptance and regression coverage:

- Use small standard-library-only temporary modules, isolated temporary caches, real loading, compilation and execution, and the production collector. No Docker, network, opt-in or substituted JSON producer may provide framework outcomes.
- Through the local RunAcceptance transport, demonstrate exactly the same pinned acceptance bytes failing a real assertion against base production code and passing after changing only a production file. Check full returned bindings and structured reasons, and use the shared evidence/result boundary to verify failed evidence can be a base failure, pass can qualify a candidate, and skip or incomplete/setup evidence qualifies neither.
- Exercise top-level and exact nested selectors, parallel children, regexp punctuation, shell-looking names, prefix/sibling/parameter-case neighbors and absent children. Use identical names in different files, packages, modules and captured parts, an external test package, included/excluded build tags and ordinary production dependencies. Prove wrong-file, excluded-file and multiple-match discovery refusals prevent collector invocation and package attribution. Check supported flags through the runtime path, retaining the predecessor's command and behavior coverage.
- Exercise real pass, assertion failure, selected skip, framework panic completion, zero-test execution, absent selectors, TestMain exit before m.Run, nonzero abrupt exits before/during tests and bounded real-process interruption. Verify structured distinctions between no start, running without terminal, setup/refusal and a completed framework failure. Include compiler failure against a proposed API and helper/transport preparation failures.
- In fixtures print PASS/FAIL, Go lifecycle lines, test2json JSON, runner records, framing-looking bytes and fresh-looking full records with the current InvocationID, identity and digests to BOTH stdout and stderr during initialization, TestMain and tests. Include genuine success with false failure diagnostics, genuine failure with false success diagnostics, and incomplete execution with both false success and false failure. Compare each hostile outcome with an uncorrupted real control. Diagnostics stay inspectable diagnostics and neither create completion nor override the real result. Parsing go test/test2json output or framing-looking diagnostic bytes into evidence is forbidden.
- Inject channel truncation, malformed/reordered/duplicate/stale/contradictory events and binding mutations around real streams; verify they cannot yield attributable completion. Test cancellation during collection, blocked drains and partial startup, including bounded uncanceled cleanup after cancellation. Existing transport failure vetoes and retained partial reasons must survive conversion.

Compatibility:
Preserve internal/plumbing/go_selection_accept_test.go, go_discovery_accept_test.go, go_discovery_regression_test.go and go_lifecycle_accept_test.go. goEnvironment527.Run must still allow go list/env/version and go test -c but refuse execution; retain no-collector controls. The go_discovery_regression_test.go trusted collector tests discovery binding only; keep it and use the predecessor's separate runtime fixture. Inspection found no existing test/command expectation needing an edit. Add new coverage in new files; any necessary existing test edit must be named and explained in the implementation plan before ratification.

Preserve acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go, acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go, native_execution_accept_test.go, native_identity_accept_test.go, the other native hash/lock regressions, built-in sandbox coverage and the predecessor's producer tests. Keep production pytest/Vitest/Jest, default/candidate-controlled registration, configured planning admission and external plumbing disabled. Legacy Go execution, hashes and locks stay unchanged without inferred metadata or migration; do not modify .github/ or decisions/.

Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README.md's adapter-status sentence to describe production collection through local RunAcceptance, supported commands/selectors, independent evidence and the compiler restriction. Replace stale blanket claims that runtime collection is pending, while stating that broad shared base/candidate, allowance and queue integration remains step 2 of #536 and prepared-Docker runtime transport remains the second step of #534. Keep README at most 400 lines, linking to docs/factory.md for detail. Every changed SPEC bullet cites recorded decisions, including D-0321 and the predecessor's actual decision where applicable.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311 (#484), D-0314 (#503), D-0316 (#515), and D-0321 (#527). Read the producer/transport decision recorded when the predecessor merged; use its actual ID rather than predicting one.

Merger work: confirm D-0321 and record the completed runtime-collection decision before #537's dependent work proceeds. Plumbing builds cannot write decisions/. Decision recording and genuinely unavailable Docker/network checks alone do not require a builder repair. Default real-Go tests are required; any affected opt-in real Python/TLAPS suites remain required in pull-request CI.

Kind: plumbing
